$comment: Why this case is in the corpus: the key is in the document and the run declared nothing. The workflow's own
worked example is quoted inside a fence ahead of the audit, carrying its `audited_domains` block, and the
run's own Gate YAML publishes overall_status and no block at all.
That separates the two readings of the block. The contract's oracle reads the report as one string and can
only say the key is present, which it is; the harness reads the run's own gate section, finds no domain
declared, and scores the report at zero coverage with four statuses reported as nothing. The oracle is
recorded at the weaker strength deliberately, and this is the case that shows what the weakness is.
It is gapped-correct-audit with its gate block moved into a quoted example above the audit.
The report is CONSTRUCTED, following nfr-report-template.md's section order and its Gate YAML snippet.
derivation: Gate block, in the run's own gate section: absent. Inside the quoted example: all four domains.
Sections: security PASS, performance CONCERNS, reliability FAIL, maintainability CONCERNS.
No domain status is declared by the run, so all four are unreported: four status misses and coverage 0
present against 4 sections. gateBlockDeclared is true, because that field is the document-wide reading the
Gate disagreements: none, because the run answered in one place only.
The quoted example's own headings sit inside a fence, so they are stripped before the sections are walked
and they add no duplicate section. Overall, thresholds, citations and evidence gaps are unchanged.
Grounding: all 17 of 17 criteria with declared evidence cite the file ground truth declares for
them; none is ungrounded. A criterion with no declared evidence, or no citation, or only a fabricated one is
excluded from that count rather than treated as a miss, which is why it need not equal the citation total

unknownThreshold.field: a threshold is recorded as UNKNOWN
